newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan non-life insurers stable in near-term - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Japan non-life insurers stable in near-term - S&P.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Wednesday it viewed the Japanese nonlife insurance sector as stable over the near term.
But it said the medium- and long-term outlook for the industry was less certain.
S&P said in a report that it believed major Japanese nonlife insurers were among the financially strongest companies in the sector worldwide.
Their financial parameters exceeded those of Japanese life insurance companies and banks and were also favourable by international comparison, it said.
The following are the claims-paying ability ratings S&P has assigned to Japanese non-life insurers:
Chiyoda Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd -- AA+
Dai-Tokyo Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd -- AA+
Dowa Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd -- AA
Mitsui Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd -- AAA
Nichido Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd -- AA+
Nippon Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd -- AA+
Sumitomo Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd -- AAA
Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd -- AAA
Yasuda Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd -- AAA
The following are the Insurance Solvency International (ISI) ratings of some non-life insurers.

The ratings are based on an analysis of each issuer's published financial statement as well as additional information in the public domain, S&P said. They do not, however, reflect in-depth meetings with senior management of the rated companies and constant surveillance is not maintained, it said.
Fuji Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd --BBB isi
Koa Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd --A isi
Nissan Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd --A isi
Nisshin Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd --A isi
Taisei Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd --A isi
Toa Fire & Marine Reinsurance Co Ltd --BBB isi
"Overall, the industry is assessed as financially strong, with asset quality high, capital sound, and catastrophe reserves largely restored," S&P said of the near-term outlook.
The assessment was based on the industry's strong rebound in its underwriting performance that began in the fiscal year from April 1994, and extended through fiscal 1995, it said.
This rebound should be sustainable over the near term in the absence of major catastrophes, S&P said.

In the near term, S&P sees a limited impact from narrower spreads on savings-type assets amid the sluggish investment environment as solid underwriting should more than offset the narrow investment spread.
S&P said, however, the medium- to long-term outlook is less certain as the repercussions of ongoing market liberalisation are not expected to be felt fully until the next century.
But it said the disparity between the first- and second-tier nonlife insurers' financial strength is expected to widen noticeably, which could lead to industry consolidation.

Small- and medium-sized firms with weak business profiles are likely to face erosion of their market share, unless they successfully implement niche strategies or align themselves with bigger companies, S&P said. While deregulation will result in a less supportive operating environment, the regulator's stance toward the industry is expected to remain accommodative by international standards, it said.
